abstract: We investigate a Zig-based balanced search structure that co-optimizes placement of contiguous node buffers across CPU and GPU memory pools. The design preserves strict height-balance and key-ordering invariants while enabling dynamic migration of sub-trees. Formal analysis shows that point and range queries, as well as insertions and rebalancings, run in $O(\log N)$ time, and that the total auxiliary memory consumption is $O(N)$. The implementation is verified by static AST inspection and by a formal invariant proof that holds for all allocation and migration operations. No empirical wall-clock measurements are reported; the evaluation relies solely on static analysis of the Zig source. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/zig-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261015_070136_understanding_nvidia_grace-bla}.
